utterances.text: Under the orders of the commander of the OZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did the commander of the North Herzegovina OZ [as interpreted] engage you -- within the North-West Herzegovina OZ, did he need an order on re-subordination from Mr. Coric or could he have done that even without that order?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, we were part of the establishment and organisation of the operation zone, and the commander of the OZ could issue an order independently to give us orders anywhere in the OZ, and he did not need any prior consent from the MP Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now tell me, please, did you participate either as a 2nd Light Assault Battalion, which was also active in this OZ, or as a 2nd MP Battalion in combat anywhere outside of your operations zone; for example, in the South-East Herzegovina OZ?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the military police under my command participated in combat in a different OZ; to be more specific, in the South-West Herzegovina OZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And now just briefly tell us what principle applied and was respected when you were sent to engage in combat outside of the North-West Herzegovina OZ; for example, in the South-East Herzegovina OZ. How did that happen, under whose orders? Could you please give us the whole system, how things functioned on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the OZ South-East Herzegovina sent a request for the engagement of additional troops to the chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. At the risk of being castigated for further interruptions, we do once again invite the answer to which part of the cross-examination this re-examination relates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic, could you perhaps tell your colleague which part of the cross-examination this re-examination relates to? MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] The entire cross-examination by Mr. Kovacic, day 1. He showed orders about re-subordination, and he asked about the principles of re-subordination. And the witness was asked to answer by just saying, Yes, or, No. This is what my re-examination refers to. I'm going to show just one of the documents from that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, for having received an explanation. On the first day of Mr. Kovacic's cross-examination, he talked about the re-subordination of light assault battalions, and my learned friend is now asking about regular battalions, and whether they were engaged in combat, and under what conditions. This re-examination doesn't have anything to do with the cross-examination as referred to by my learned friend Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to put the following question. I don't want to go over the same ground again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: The principle that you have just described for the active-duty battalion, did the same principle apply to the 2nd Light Assault Battalion? And then you will continue on from where you left it off. We left it off with a request to the chief of the Main Staff, but before that, tell me whether the same principle applied.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, madam, the same principle applied, irrespective of the battalion, whether it was an active-duty or a light-assault battalion. Let me respond to Ms. Alaburic and say that there were no so-called active-duty battalions. They were either active or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Andabak, let's continue. We left it off with the part where you said that the commander of the OZ that needed you - in this case it was South-East Herzegovina - sent a request to the chief of the Main Staff. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of the Main Staff issued an order to the MP Administration for the redeployment of troops and units, and he informed the OZ from which we were being sent about that same order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When a light-assault battalion or an active-duty battalion of the military police arrived in a different operations zone, for example, South-East Herzegovina, who did you report to and who was your commander there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, there we reported to the OZ commander. He then re-subordinated us to a commander in the territory where the -- where we were deployed and whose area of responsibility that was. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Andabak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. May I just make something -- make sure about something you said. You said that the Chief of the General Staff would order the chief of the Military Police Administration to do this or that; he, himself, not via the chief of the Defence Department, but directly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, directly, and everything is based on the Chief of the Main Staff and the order by the Chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Now may we have on e-court document -- it's a document that the Petkovic Defence showed you during the examination-in -- I mean the cross-examination. 4D02056 is the number. And at the same time, those who have a hard copy can look at document -- well, that includes you, Witness. You'll have one document on your screen and one document in front of you. P00143 is the second document I'd like you to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, we have on our screens what the Defence of General Petkovic -- did I -- document P00143, what it put in its document, it is provisional instructions for the work of the MP units of the HVO, dated April 1992. And let's look at item 1 there: "Within the HVO, the Military Police establishment shall be organised within the HVO, and it shall control and command all military police units belonging to operative groups, organisational units, and the Military Police Administration itself." We also have items 4 and 5. But you have P00143, which is the original document in front of you as well, and I'm going to read out some points from that document which are not contained in this summary, in this two-sentence summary extracted from document P00143. I'm going to read item 6 first in the general provisions section. It says: "Military police units," or, rather, their commanders, "shall carry out all MP tasks and assignments pursuant to a request from the commander of the unit of the HVO under whose composition they act -- within whose composition they act." Now, Mr. Andabak, tell me this, and you've already said this before, I believe: Who gave you your daily tasks and assignments? Who issued you your daily tasks and assignments?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, we received daily tasks and assignments from the commander of the operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you receive them in the form of a request, which you could refuse, or in the form of an order, which you, if you were a soldier, you were not allowed to refuse?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the form of an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now let's look at item 9 in that same document, and it wasn't contained in the 4D document. Item 9 reads as follows: "The Military Police Administration of the HVO is responsible for the situation and professional training and combat readiness of the MP units. "It follows, monitors, and studies the organisation and establishment of military police units, and exercises control, and assesses the level of training and combat readiness of the MP units. Therefore, similarly, the HVO proposes measures for their improvement and replenishment. "The Military Police administration shall also draw conclusions from the experiences gained in the work of the military police and its units and incorporates them into the training of the military police units." Now let's look at item 10, the selection of soldiers: "Soldiers for the replenishment of military police units shall be selected according to special standards and criteria set by the Military Police Administration and the SIS and HVO administrations." Item 11: "The Military Police Administration shall be responsible for furnishing military police units with military police equipment and military police insignia while the command of the parent unit, as part of which a given military police unit was formed, shall be responsible for the acquisition of weapons and other materiel and technical equipment." Mr. Andabak, you said several times, because we had an entire discussion during the examination about the responsibilities of the MP Administration, control and command of military police units by the MP Administration, you spoke about administrative tasks, instructions, and guide-lines, and so on, and you said that that was something that the MP Administration issued orders to you about. Now, when you said that, did you mean all those points that I read out, and was that the situation in practice?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel, that's how it was. As it is set out in this document, that's how it was in practice, the responsibility of the MP police on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, on page 2 of 4D2056, we see P00837. That's the first document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before my learned friend continues, I'd just like to object to these questions, for the record, because the document that we're talking about now relates exclusively to the functions of control and command exercised by the Military Police Administration according to its rules and regulations, and at no point in time did I mean to say that the MP Administration did not have other tasks. So if my learned friend wants to talk about these other tasks, I think that's a waste of time, because we've all had those documents and we were all able to read through them. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] There's no problem there. I'll ask a direct question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did the MP Administration control or command in any other way, except giving instructions and guide-lines, on the subjects that we've just discussed under items 9, 10, and 11?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, the Military Police Administration never ordered military police units -- issued orders to military police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let's repeat this again. Who issued orders to you on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground, it was the commander of the operative zone in whose area I was located who issued orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And who was -- who did the commander of the operative zone get his orders from?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the chief of the Main Staff who issued orders to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Andabak, thank you. Now let's look at page 2, and P00837 is the document that is quoted; that is, instructions for the work of the military police units. And it is dated November 1992, and only three items, I believe, are mentioned there as well. Mr. Andabak, I'm not going to go back to this document. We've already seen it during the examination-in-chief. But tell me this: These instructions, did they change anything in relation to control and command of the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything stayed the same, just as it was set out in the first set of instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: On that same page, we have an excerpt from the military police establishment, and you'll find it in your binder. It is document P00957. In that document -- or, rather, a sentence was extracted from that document, and it says that: "The Military Police Administration controls and commands all MP units." Before we look at this document 957 in the original, tell me whether anything changed with respect to control and command of the military police on the ground with this kind of establishment and organisation.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this organisation, the only change was that the 1st Active-Duty Battalion was formed, which was directly linked to the MP Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right. When you say it was directly in contact or connected with the MP Administration, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the unit could go into action in all the operative zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And who gave the order for a unit to enter an operative zone?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Military Police Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Does the MP Administration issue the order at its own initiative or was the procedure different?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure was as I described it earlier on. There was a legitimate request from the commander of the operative zone where the unit was to be sent, so once again the line is: The Main Staff, and then the Main Staff issues an order to the MP Administration to deploy men to the operative zone to carry out the assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And when this 1st Active-Duty Battalion arrives in the operative zone, who is in charge of it there, who commands it there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion, when it arrives, is also commanded by the commander of the operative zone whose area of responsibility it is, and they act according to his instructions exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now, I want to ask you about something else, briefly. You -- well, in response to a question from the Petkovic Defence on page 34 of yesterday's transcript, you said the following: You said that the platoons of the brigade military police were abolished and that you think that there was a new organisation put in place. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the fourth document in your binder - the document number is P07018 - and it says "The Ministry of Defence." The date is the 3rd of December, 1993, and it says: "The Military Police Administration establishment thus far was not efficacious, functional, operational, and efficient." And then it goes on to say: "I hereby order: "1. Immediately undertake the establishment of the following MP units." In item 2, it says that: "The military police battalions attached to brigades, HVO brigades, cease to be within the composition of the HVO brigades and become part of the 2nd and 3rd Battalion of the Military Police of the HVO." Tell us now, please, Mr. Andabak, is this the kind of establishment and organisation you had in mind in this document, and it's dated the 3rd of December, 1993, when you were speaking about the new type of organisation?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel, but I couldn't remember the exact period, the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel, to interrupt you. I would only like to ask the following questions. When we speak about the orders, we, of course, know that, as a whole, the police -- military police was mainly responsible for two major tasks, according to my opinion, at least; that is, to maintain law and order in the given military zone -- operative zone, and, on the other hand, as a number-two task, they were also taken and ordered to participate in the actual battle, battle-field, and to do their duties while there. Now, my question is the following: that when we speak about the orders in general, could we -- or could the witness distinguish between two sets of orders, that is, number 1, related to the maintenance of law and order, and, on the other hand, were there orders which related only to their tasks in the battle-field, that is, the military duties? It is my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well, one could say that there were two types of orders. However, in our daily execution of duties, we only received one single order which applied to combat or, for example, an order to escort a convoy, or that something had to be let through. All that fell within the scope of one single order applying to the OZ. For example, the 2nd Company would be sent into combat, and the other companies would be sent to the check-points, to step up patrols in the town because the situation had deteriorated with respect to law and order or the number of crimes committed, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: And in this connection, then, your answer, that this order always came from the Main Staff, isn't it what you have already stated? That is, in a single order which you referred to, that single order, orders, have always been given by the Main Staff; is it what you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I was on the ground, I received orders from the OZ commander, and the OZ commander most probably received some of the orders from the chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: Very well, Mr. Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And now I would like us to look at a few orders with respect to the control and command. They are in your binder. We will start with an order which you will find in your binder as the sixth document from the beginning. I am going to be asking you whether you received the order and whether you executed that order. This is an order issued by the Main Staff. I apologise. P00377 is the number, an order issued by the Main Staff on the 10th of August, 1992. This is a ban on the entrance of military formations into the zone of responsibility. This was sent to all commands -- to all military police commands and to all civilian police commands, and underneath it says: "To be delivered to Livno." Did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received this order via the command of the OZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you execute this order?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We executed and reported back to the OZ commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: We can skip one document in order to avoid wasting time. Could we now see number P00458. This was issued on the 8th of September, 1992, again by the Main Staff. And it says in the document: "I order all humanitarian aid convoys are to be allowed to go through, and, if necessary, they should be secured by police forces. "No humanitarian aid transport should be checked if not approved by the HVO Main Staff." Item 5: "The HVO command is obliged to immediately solve any misunderstanding and irresponsible conduct of individuals. "Military police and civilian police commands should be informed about this order." Mr. Andabak, did anybody inform you about this order? If, Yes, who was it, and did you act upon this order, did you execute it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the OZ commander briefed us about this order, Mr. Siljeg did, during one of the briefings. I, as a battalion commander, informed the check-points. I related the order word for word to them, and then I reported back to the OZ commander about the execution of the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Again we can skip a document, and let's look at the following one, which is P01673, another document from the Main Staff. This is dated 16 March 1993. It was sent to all OZs, to the military police, and to special-purpose units. It says: "A ban on the use of HVO units for military police assignments." Tell me, please, did you ever see this order before?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw it in the OZ command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. And now let's go -- THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] A technical intervention, if I may, please. Your Honours, just a technical intervention, please. When it came to the first order, I believe that it was sent by the -- that the witness became the battalion commander in November, and as we go on, he was no longer battalion commander, he was in Ljubuski. Could we please be more precise and say exactly what he saw and what he didn't?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have already drew your attention to the fact that over a long period of time in 1993, this witness performed other functions. He was not the commander of the 2nd Battalion, and the same applies to the dates of all the orders. So all the questions [as interpreted] by this witness are very questionable in his capacity as the commander of the 2nd Battalion. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, just one more intervention, if I may, please. My colleague Mr. Coric has already used the word "the so-called counsel" for my counsel, and I don't think that's fair. Your Honour, I believe that it is a lesser insult than if somebody calling my entire unit "the so-called unit." Please, I believe that it is not fair, on the part of my learned -- of my friend Coric, to call my counsel "the so-called counsel."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Ms. Alaburic. My remarks concerning Defence counsel also apply to the accused. Let's avoid people being incriminated here. What we are interested in is the merits of the case. Mr. Coric, if someone said "the so-called lawyer," that is not acceptable, because lawyers are fully-fledged lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just want to say that I did hear what Mr. Coric said behind my back. And for the integrity of my client and my own integrity, I would like this to be recorded. I heard the comments made by Mr. Coric. He made comments over the past few months many times, but I didn't feel the need to react. I understand that he is in an exceptional situation now and finds it difficult to control his own actions, so I understand. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm going to address counsel as "Dr. Alaburic," and not "Counsel," because I see that she has some opinions about my mental health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic, you may proceed. I believe Colonel Andabak had something to say. Mr. Andabak, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, General Petkovic is saying an untruth here, just as is Ms. Alaburic. So the previous document was the 8th of September, 1992, and I was the commander of the 2nd Battalion -- or, rather, assistant chief of the MP Administration for the operative zone. And as I've already said, I co-ordinated between -- I acted as co-ordinator between the 2nd Light Assault and 6th Military Police Battalions. I'm the person who received orders from the commander of the operative zone, and I then issued orders down the line to my subordinates in the operative zone for execution of the orders. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: To avoid any misunderstandings, Mr. Andabak, could you tell us what post you held in September 1992, because we're dealing with September 1992, the document mentioned by Mr. Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Military Police Battalion of the Operative Zone of North-West Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, this last document is dated March 1993, when the gentleman was head of the General and Traffic Police Section. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Mr. Andabak, would you look at the previous document, dated the 16th of March, 1993, and tell us why you said -- and have you seen -- why you said what you said, and have you seen the document? And if you have, in what capacity did you see it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Counsel, it was only at the end of March that I came to the post of assistant chief, and with the hand-over of duty and take-over of duty, and because of battalion -- combat assignments. And later on, my functional duty was chief of the Department for General and Traffic MP, so that I acted as co-ordinator and co-ordinated with all the units in the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna of the day; the military police ones, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Fine, Mr. Andabak. Now look at the next document, which is P02911.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. There's perhaps something which you have forgotten to mention. Colonel, the document 1673, if I understood correctly, on the 16th of March you were still heading the 2nd Battalion. Had you seen this document at the time, document P01673?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I have seen the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all I wanted to know. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now let's look at P02911 next, please. This is a Main Staff document dated the 22nd of June, 1993, and it refers to the engagement of forces in Prozor. It was sent to the brigades and to the military police, Valentin Coric -- to Valentin Coric, and it says: "In order to ensure the defence of Prozor from the Muslim forces, bring in urgently in the course of the day:" And then in item 5, it says: "Military police - 80 to 100 men." Mr. Andabak, when you spoke about the orders from the Main Staff that were addressed to the MP Administration, linked to the deployment of MP units in other zones, is this the kind of order you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel, this is one of those orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document, which is 5D05117. The document is a Main Staff document for the forward command post of Prozor. The registration number is 2/93, and please remember that number. It says: "Examine the UNHCR convoy and the MCK." It was sent to the Command of the North-West Herzegovina Operative Zone/Military Police, and it says: "I hereby order:" Now look at page 2 of that document. It's a document of the forward command post of the Operative Zone of North-West Herzegovina, as we've said, and it says: "Conveying the order received from the HVO Main Staff," and the reference number is 2/93; reference number 2/93, forward the order received from the HVO Main Staff. Now, Mr. Andabak, did you receive this order, and have you ever seen it before? Did you see it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll be very specific. Looking at the date and the duty that I performed in both -- both in February and in July, I was in the operative zone on assignment as battalion commander and as assistant chief of the Military Police Administration, which means that these orders referred to the command of the operative zone and the military police, which means that we received these orders from the commander of the operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Fine, Mr. Andabak. Let's move on to the next document. It is P06825, once again a Main Staff document dated the 23rd of November, 1993, sent to the military districts and forward command post in Prozor. It is an order which relates to the convoy carrying humanitarian aid and its passage, free passage for the convoy. Have you seen this order before, Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this order, too, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. Now we're going to skip a document and move on to P03889, which is a document put to you by the Petkovic Defence. From this document -- well, you were shown a portion of that document - you don't have to read the whole of it - a part which is to be found on page 4, last paragraph. And in the English, it's page 6, second paragraph from the bottom. Before I go on to the document, I'm going to ask you the following: During the cross-examination of the Stojic Defence -- by the Stojic Defence, you responded to questions linked to your departure on the 30th of June to Mostar, and this was recorded on transcript page 50973. You said that you arrived in Mostar on the 30th of June, at the invitation of Mr. Petkovic and pursuant to his order. Now, before we look at the document, could you tell me how -- in what way did Mr. Petkovic invite you to attend? Did he use a courier, did he send a written order?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we clear up what post the witness held and what post he was in when he came to Mostar on the 30th of June? MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Only if the Trial Chamber wishes to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But tell me, Mr. Andabak, how did he invite you? I mean, technically, how did he invite you?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called me up on the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now look at the page I mentioned, and it was shown to you by the Petkovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were called over the phone. What was your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was chief of the Department for General and Traffic Police Affairs. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: It says here: "In this fighting --" this was put to you by the Petkovic Defence: "In this fighting in Mostar, members of the Livno military police," et cetera. Now, when that was put to you by the Petkovic Defence, you said that what it says here was incorrect, whereas this is your report, so I'm interested in knowing why you said it's not correct. Can you explain that to me?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that it was not correct because the counsel just wanted to hear a yes-or-no answer. Had I said, Yes, or had I said, No, I would not have been allowed to explain at all how and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right. Fine, Mr. Andabak. Can you explain to us now why?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, I was first called up by the defence minister to send a unit. And as I said, I -- as I said earlier, I had a problem with the command of the operative zone about sending a unit, because the command of the operative zone said some ugly things about it, about that. And then General Petkovic phoned later, and I acted upon orders, because I thought that the situation had been resolved between the operative zone and the HVO's staff and headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Andabak. Now, on that same page, the Petkovic Defence asked you to focus on an excerpt which says that in Gornji Vakuf, with the military police of Livno, that there was Mr. Rade Lavric there too, who was at the time Mr. Coric's deputy. Now, to avoid any misunderstandings, I'm going to ask you a direct question. Who issued orders to you when you were in Gornji Vakuf on assignment? Who did you receive your orders from?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Gornji Vakuf, I received orders from the brigade commander of Gornji Vakuf mostly, and as battalion commander, I was in the operative zone fairly frequently, where I reported on my combat operations, and I was given certain assignments from the commander of the operative zone as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Andabak. Now, during the cross-examination by the Petkovic Defence, you were asked about disarmament and the isolation of Muslims in Livno in July 1993. And the Prosecutor also asked you questions about that today. And the Prosecution and I, too, showed you the same report by Mr. Tucak, so let's look at the next document, which is 5D05094. This order was issued on the 21st of July, 1993 by the brigade commander, Stanko Vrgoc. Did you receive this order? Could you just have a look at it? Look at the first part of this order, where it says: "Together with the Ferdo Sucic Battalion, Tactical Group 1 of our brigade is to begin to disarm and search for facilities held by Muslims along the Podhum-Golinjevo axis, bring in all men of between 16 and 60 years of age, except for the disabled and war victims, and requisition all weapons ..." Did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So far, you've mentioned several times that you acted upon the brigade orders or the brigade order. Is that the order that you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the order that I had in mind. And as I've already told you, I acted upon the order received from the commander of the Petar Kresimir IV Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Andabak. The Praljak Defence showed you document P03068. I don't want to call it up. I'm saying this just for the transcript. The document is dated 1st of July, 1993. It was Mr. Coric's order which concerned the military police unit under the command of Mr. Perica Turalija. The date on the order was the 1st of July. Could you please look at the following document in your binder, which is 5D04394. The document is dated 31st July 1993, which means 30 days after the previous document issued by Mr. Coric. It is titled "Instructions to the MP Administration," signed by a commander, Brigadier General Slobodan Praljak, and it was sent to the Military Police Administration in Mostar, to Mr. Valentin Coric personally. And it says "Perica Turalija," and the document reads as follows. I'm going to read the first two paragraphs: "The order you issued on the 29th of July, 1993, number," so on and so forth, I don't want to read the whole number, "on the suspension of the MP platoon commander, Perica Turalija, and his relief of duty, will not be implemented. "Perica Turalija's MP platoon is under my operational command, and it is carrying out all tasks assigned to it." Tell me, please, Mr. Andabak, do you know that after the 31st of July, Perica Turalija's platoon was in Prozor, performing tasks under the operative command of the commander, Brigadier General Slobodan Praljak?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Counsel, Perica Turalija continued to discharge the duties of the 3rd Active-Duty Company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. And now let's look at the last document in this set, which is P00721. This document was shown to you by the Prosecutor. It is a document issued by the Municipal Staff of Prozor on the 8th of November, 1992. This is a report. Somewhere in the middle of the report, it says: "For the aforementioned reasons, the command is working on appointing a new military police commander." Mr. Andabak, do you know which military police commander this refers to? Did they appoint anybody or not? Do you know what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Counsel, the command was not happy with the work of the then commander, Mr. Jozo Mestrovic, and they were seeking possibilities to replace him and bring in a new person. As far as I know, Mr. Ilija Franjic came later and replaced him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Andabak. We will no longer need any documents, and I have just a few more questions to ask you. If you remember, yesterday the Prosecutor showed you P01130, which is a handwritten document issued by the SIS of the 3rd Brigade. Do you remember that? And you answered the Prosecutor that the 3rd Brigade most probably was in Gornji Vakuf in January. Tell me, please, did you see the 3rd Brigade in Gornji Vakuf in January?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Counsel, I saw one part of the brigade. I don't know what establishment of that brigade it was. They were deployed around a place called Pidris, in the direction towards the entrance into Gornji Vakuf, a little before Uzricje, on that side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Andabak, yesterday you were asked about another document at great length when the unit returned to Livno and then celebrated at the bus-stop by shooting in the air. Tell me, did you participate in the war against the Serbs? I'm referring to units from Livno.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes, we did, Counsel, from the very beginning in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. And when you returned from combat missions after having fought against the Serbs, did you celebrate in the same manner?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the military police units, but all units. There was shooting in every village.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Andabak. And now just very briefly with regard to the Stojic Defence questions, just for the transcript, I would like to say that you were shown document P01615. I don't want to call it up. And that document concerned your visit to the Heliodrom and the investigation of the meat [indiscernible]. The number of the document is P01615. According to that document, that was in March 1993. Did you go to Heliodrom again or was that your only visit to the barracks at Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I believe that I did go once again to inspect the work of the military police at the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what season was it? Was it before the summer of 1993, before May, after May 1993? If you don't remember, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I can't answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. In answering questions about that document, referring to releasing a person from the prison, a member of an HVO unit, on page 50978 of the LiveNote, it has been recorded that you said that the prison in Ljubuski was under the military police at the time. And then on page 50979, you said, about the same matter, that you did not have any responsibility over that soldier or the prisons held by the brigade military police. In that respect, could you please tell us, and can we clarify this matter, do you know who secured the prison in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, it is certainly an error in interpretation. The prison in Ljubuski was secured by the brigade military police from Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And who was in command of that brigade military police in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsel, the commander was the brigade commander. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Andabak. Your Honours, this brings my re-examination to an end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Andabak, your testimony has just ended. I would like to thank you, and personally and on behalf of my colleagues, for having come at the request of Mr. Valentin Coric to take the stand. I wish you a safe journey home, and I shall ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you will allow me, I would also like to thank you, the OTP, the Defence teams defending the accused. And, finally, I would like to say that in the courtroom I don't see people who speak behind people's backs when those same people are not here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's really just this: I suppose, you could say, in English, "put down a marker."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We do note, and perhaps we're advising the Trial Chamber to ponder and everybody to ponder before we get further witnesses, but we do know that the practice adopted in relation to the length of the re-examination appears to be very different from the practice that was consistently adopted during the Petkovic Defence case, where we were -- we were generally invited to indicate how long we would be, and then, for practical purposes, were held to that figure, with, of course, from time to time modest extensions. That hasn't happened here. It was a long re-examination. We'll all, in due course, be examining the content of it, so I say nothing at all about that, but it does seem that a rather different practice has been adopted, and this is a -- well, it's a preliminary protest, really, and a hope that there will be a consistent practice applied in relation to this accused consistently with the practice that was applied in relation to our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Next week, if I understand correctly, two witnesses are going to come and testify. The witnesses will be at the disposal of the Chamber. Ms. Tomic. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] As things stand now, they should be here, and they are not two, but three. They're all 92 ter witnesses, and there's three of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give me the names again so that I can check with the documents that I have? MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The first one is protected, and his pseudonym -- I don't know, Judge Trechsel. Should we go into private session and I shall say the name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was verbally expressing the pseudonym, which is, "NO." MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It has been a long and hard day, and a joke will not go amiss. The first witness's pseudonym is NO, and the other two are Mate Jelcic and Pero Nikolic. I have their schedule before me. The first one is NO, the second one is Mate Jelcic, and, finally, Pero Nikolic.
